Digital, Inclusive and Accessible (DIA) Service Provision 2023-2027

description.narrative: DIA-projektet syftar till att fortsätta stödja den pågående digitaliseringsprocessen i Ukraina i syfte att stärka regeringens kapacitet att leverera högkvalitativa och tillgängliga digitala tjänster till utsatta grupper i Ukraina samtidigt som digital teknik och lösningar används för att möta andra komplexa utmaningar som kriget medför. inklusive att säkerställa öppenhet och ansvarsskyldighet för återhämtningsprocessen, vilket är avgörande för Ukrainas EU-integration.

The DIA Project aims to continue supporting the ongoing digitalisation process in Ukraine with the view of strengthening the Government’s capacities to deliver high quality and accessible digital services to vulnerable groups in Ukraine while using digital technologies and solutions to address other complex challenges posed by the war, including ensuring transparency and accountability of the recovery process, critically important for Ukraine’s EU Integration.

title.narrative: Agreement Digital, Inclusive and Accessible (DIA) Service Provision 2023-2027
Decision Digital, Inclusive and Accessible (DIA) Service Provision

description.narrative:
The overall result of the DIA Support Project reflects substantial progress in strengthening Ukraines digital public service infrastructure, with a particular focus on inclusion, accessibility, and responsiveness to wartime needs.
Some examples of results:
A total of 16 new digital services and tools were launched during the reporting period. These services were developed to address the specific needs of Ukrainian citizens, including war veterans, internally displaced persons, and other vulnerable groups. Among them are:
- A service enabling the issuance of extracts from the Unified State Register of War Veterans at Administrative Service Centres (TSNAPs), reducing processing time from 30 days to 5 minutes. - Digital applications for war-related disability status and recognition of family members of deceased defenders, available both online via the Diia platform and offline through TSNAP administrators. - A service allowing students under the age of 23, who are children of fallen defenders, to apply for state-funded tuition compensation for higher education. - A tool for entrepreneurs to digitally request changes to their business plans under the state microgrant programme, including adjustments to product types and pricing.
A total of 18,301 civil servants completed the Digitalisation in Public Sector training programme. Participant feedback indicated high levels of satisfaction and practical relevance.
The Womens Leadership Programme was relaunched, engaging 25 female civil servants from national and regional institutions in structured leadership development activities.
The TSNAP Monitoring Course, incorporating modules on barrier-free access and inclusion, reached final production stage. Public launch is scheduled for October 2025. (TSNAP are Administrative Service Centres in Ukraine, one-stop shops for citizens to access a wide range of public administrative services.)
The Digital Accessibility Competence Centre (DACC) was formally established and began providing expert consultations, training, and accessibility audits to public authorities. Accessibility audits were conducted for key platforms, including the Ministry of Social Policy website and Unified State Web Portal of Electronic Services. These platforms were upgraded to comply with WCAG 2.1 standards.
Targeted training sessions were delivered to: National Police of Ukraine, Pension Fund of Ukraine (Vinnytsia region) and Local authorities in Kirovohrad, Poltava, Mykolaiv, and Dnipropetrovsk regions. These activities enhanced institutional capacity to implement digital accessibility standards.
The Unified Web Portal of Executive Authorities was technically upgraded to meet national accessibility standards.
The Diia mobile application underwent an accessibility audit. A technical specification was developed to address identified gaps, with implementation planned by the end of 2025.
Expert input contributed to the development and adoption of several legislative and regulatory instruments, including: Cabinet of Ministers Resolution No. 574 on mine action procedures, Draft resolution on basic social assistance, Regulatory impact analysis for draft legislation on digital accessibility
Technical support was provided to advance the National Strategy for a Barrier-Free Environment, with emphasis on digital inclusion.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
